svg.aria-label: Pin destination reference for the three LTV-847 optocouplers on the RPI-BC input board, seen from the component side. Each of the sixteen pins per chip is labelled with its pin number, leg letter, matrix hole and the point it connects to. No traces are drawn.

g.text: RPi I/O board — optocoupler pin destinations, COMPONENT side (no traces)
Three LTV-847 DIP-16. Chips and sockets sit on this face; nothing is wired here. Sheet 1 of 2.
COMPONENT SIDE (front) — chips facing you, Pi header columns on the LEFT, plug edge away from you
IC-A rows 8 & 11 · channels 1-4 = CHIL · BLR · DHW · ZV
IC-B rows 13 & 16 · channels 1-3 = DEHUM · BOS2 · BOS1 · ch4 dark
IC-C rows 18 & 21 · spares SP-A · SP-B · SP-D · SP-C — NOTCH REVERSED
IC-C IS ROTATED 180° — its C/E row faces the row-17 ground rail
K = LED cathode → 4.7 kΩ resistor → plug pin (field side)
C = collector → Pi GPIO access pad
unused (channel built, no plug position behind it)
IC-C is notch-opposite to IC-A and IC-B. Check its notch before inserting the chip — reversing it is the likeliest assembly mistake on this board.
Pi nn = physical header position (1-40). BCM nn = the Broadcom GPIO number — the same line, and the number config.yml keys its inputs by (numbering: "bcm").
Holes are the canonical component-side (column,row) on both sheets, so a hole label means the same physical hole in either view — only its screen position mirrors.
